# Multiple small shell additions: exact anchor credit and an exposure LP

This note proves an exact multiple-addition law when all additions
share one anchor, an all-direction credit bound for each anchor in
general, and finite linear-program certificates for upper bounds.
An actual six-base example shows that a binary full/empty exposure
cost is not the true first-order depth coefficient: a minimizing
cap can take proper portions of two nonowned fibers.

Let T be a full d-simplex, d>=2, with volume V, centroid g,
Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d, and barycentric coordinates lambda_0,...,lambda_d.
Write b=1/(d+1), h=1-b. Absolute mixed depth A_mu(y) is the infimum
of mu(H) over all closed ambient halfspaces containing the actual
source point y; normalized depth is A_mu(y)/mu(S).

The core fibers at all vertices of Q={0,1}^n are exactly T.
Outside positive-volume fibers are A_p at a finite set O of integer
bases in [-1,2]^n minus Q. Set a_p=|A_p|, E=sum_p a_p. These are
ACTUAL fibers of one convex body, not independent assigned traces.
The archive candidate 8a123edc8f6439bd
proves A_p subset T and proves that E<2^(-d)V forces every nonempty
integer fiber into this shell. Here shell membership may instead
be imposed directly; that classification is not a new claim.

Each p has a unique anchor q(p)=clamp(p,0,1) in Q and distinct
partner v(p)=2q(p)-p in Q. For q in Q put

    E_q=sum_{p:q(p)=q} a_p.

Use rho_d from candidate 1d1be0b22c707856:
for a continuous unit normal u, with B=u.g and ell=min_T u.x,

    f(u)=|T intersect {u.x>=B}|/V,
    R(u)=|T intersect {u.x>=2B-ell}|/V,
    rho_d=min_u [f(u)-Gamma+R(u)]>0.                 (1)

That note proves all continuity and equality-direction details,
and gives rho_2=2(sqrt(10)-3)/9. This is a sufficient profile
threshold, not the optimal geometric mass range.

## 1. Full aggregate credit at one anchor

For every q with E_q<=rho_d V,

    A_mu((q,g)) >= Gamma V+E_q.                     (2)

Proof. A nonvertical cap through (q,g) has margin

    u.(x-g)+beta.(z-q)>=0.

If every owned A_p is fully captured, their contribution is E_q.
Otherwise choose one owned p whose trace is not full. The affine
thresholds at p and v(p) add to 2B. The threshold at p must be
strictly greater than ell; hence the threshold in its core partner
is strictly less than 2B-ell, and that partner contributes at
least R(u)V. Thus, using the SAME original cap,

    mu(H) >= V[f(u)+min(E_q/V,R(u))]
          >= Gamma V+E_q.                           (3)

No partner is counted twice: this proof either takes all owned
fibers, or takes a single core partner. Other fibers are ignored.
If no fiber is owned, the ordinary own-fiber bound suffices.

A vertical through-point cap contains the entire own T. This
also suffices, since rho_d is at most its value at a canonical
normal, ((d-1)/(d+1))^d<Gamma, and 2Gamma<1. A containing cap
contains a parallel through-point cap. These observations handle
all ambient closed halfspaces, including vertical boundaries.

The conclusion improves the archived small-total-additions OC
bound to an exact unnormalized anchor credit. It does not assert
that all nonowned additions can be discarded by one common tilt.

## 2. Exact law for arbitrarily many additions with one anchor

Choose a nonempty set P of shell bases, all with the same anchor q.
Assign ANY positive convex A_p subset T, and let E=sum_P |A_p|.
Take the convex hull of these fibers and the binary core. If
E<=rho_d V, its exact maximum and unique maximizing point are

    max A_mu=Gamma V+E,  unique maximizer (q,g),
    max depth_mu=(Gamma+E/V)/(2^n+E/V).              (4)

There is no mutual shape constraint beyond A_p subset T.

Here is the actual compatibility check. Flip integer coordinates
to make q=0; then P is a subset of {-1,0}^n minus {0}.
An outside integer point of conv(Q union P) has a coordinate -1.
That forces its convex representation entirely onto points of P
having that coordinate -1. All remaining integer coordinates are
0 or -1, so their extremality in the negative binary cube forces
every point in the representation to be the same p. Consequently
the exact integer projection is Q union P. Every p is exposed:
if S={i:p_i=-1}, the linear functional with coefficients -(n+1)
on S and +1 off S has its unique maximum at p, with gap at least
one on every other point of Q union P. Its continuous fiber is
therefore exactly A_p. All continuous generators lie in T and
each core generator is T, so the core fibers remain exactly T.
The ambient convex hull is full dimensional.

For the upper bound at q use delta_q(z)=sum_i z_i. It is positive
on Q minus {q}, and at most -1 on every p. The d+1 caps

    lambda_i(x)-2 delta_q(z)>=b                     (5)

each have mass Gamma V+E and cover the own fiber and ALL additions.
They exclude every other core fiber. At y!=g in the own fiber,
choose lambda_i(y)>b and replace b by lambda_i(y) in (5). Its
mass is strictly less than Gamma V+E.

Every other core vertex w is still exposed. The affine functional

    delta_w(z)=(n+1) sum_{i:w_i=1}(1-z_i)
                          +sum_{i:w_i=0} z_i

vanishes at w and is at least one at every other core vertex and
every point of P. At p it is at least (n+1)|supp(w)|-n>=1.
The caps lambda_i-2delta_w>=b isolate that core's canonical caps,
each of mass Gamma V; they cover the fiber. Finally an exposed
vertical cap isolates each p and has mass a_p<Gamma V+E.
Together with (2), this proves (4), including uniqueness and a
finite original-cap upper cover. Thus if E=tW+o(t), the exact
normalized right derivative is W(2^n-Gamma)/(4^n V).

## 3. A finite support-dependent directional exposure certificate

Return to arbitrary O and fix a core q. Flip coordinates so q=0,
and denote the transformed outside bases again by p. For canonical
direction i define U_{p,i}=max_{x in A_p} lambda_i(x).
For a subset Z of outside fibers required to have ZERO cap mass,
consider the finite feasibility LP in eta in R^n:

    eta_j>=h                    for j=1,...,n,
    eta.p>=U_{p,i}-b             for p in Z.         (6)

Whenever it is feasible, the actual cap

    H={lambda_i(x)-eta.z>=b}

has own mass Gamma V, zero mass on every other core fiber, and
zero mass on each A_p with p in Z. Supporting equalities in (6)
are permitted: A_p has positive d-volume, so its supporting plane
has zero d-volume. Therefore the exact finite optimization

    Omega_{q,i}=min_{Z satisfying (6)} sum_{p notin Z} a_p

gives the rigorous upper certificate

    A_mu((q,g)) <= Gamma V+min_i Omega_{q,i}.         (7)

The optimum is over finitely many subsets, each tested by an
ordinary real LP. It need not equal the actual added cap cost:
uncertified fibers may be partially captured.

There is an exact dual infeasibility certificate. System (6)
is feasible if and only if, for every gamma_j>=0 and mu_p>=0
with p ranging over Z such that

    sum_j gamma_j e_j+sum_p mu_p p=0,

one has

    h sum_j gamma_j+sum_p mu_p(U_{p,i}-b)<=0.        (8)

This is the ordinary finite Farkas alternative, with all rows
and signs displayed. In particular, unlike duplicating caps,
this condition retains the shared integer tilt eta exactly.

## 4. A base-only piecewise-linear exposure cost and depth bracket

A shape-independent version is useful for first-order accounting.
For positive weights a=(a_p), define chi_q(a) to be the minimum
sum_{p in F} a_p over F subset O for which there is eta satisfying

    eta_j>=1 for all j,  eta.p>=1 for p in O minus F. (9)

Equivalently q is strictly exposed among all the other core bases
and all the outside bases that have not been discarded into F.
The criterion is affine-coordinate invariant under the preceding
cube flips. The exact dual of (9) is the absence of a nonzero
nonnegative dependence among its row vectors, since all right
sides are one. Thus this is a finite combinatorial/LP invariant.
It is a minimum of finitely many linear forms in a, homogeneous,
continuous, and piecewise linear. Every owned p must lie in F,
because p=2q-v would otherwise require both eta.p and eta.v
positive. Hence

    E_q<=chi_q(a)<=E.                               (10)

Taking 2eta as the actual cap tilt excludes all certified fibers,
uniformly over A_p subset T and over canonical directions. At ANY
y in the core fiber q choose lambda_i(y)>=b. The corresponding
cap has mass at most Gamma V+chi_q(a). No attainment or compactness
claim about arbitrary optimizing cap normals is needed.

If E<=rho_d V, then every anchor satisfies (2), and the maximum
over actual source points obeys the exact bracket

    Gamma V+max_q E_q <= max A_mu
                      <= Gamma V+max_q chi_q(a).    (11)

For the upper bound outside the core, an outside shell point has
some coordinate -1 or 2. The vertical cap at that integer level
misses the whole core and has mass at most E<Gamma V. Any additional
zero-volume fiber has depth zero: its base cannot lie in the convex
hull of positive-volume bases, since positive Minkowski interpolation
would then give it positive volume, and a strict base separator
gives a zero-mass vertical cap. Thus (11) accounts for deterministic
centers everywhere in the actual mixed source.

If a_p(t)=t omega_p+o(t) with a fixed finite support, then
chi_q(a(t))=t chi_q(omega)+o(t). Formula (11) gives genuine uniform
first-order bounds without any assumed diameter or convergence
rate for A_p(t). In general its upper coefficient is not exact.
The next actual source certifies the obstruction.

## 5. Six actual bases: partial traces defeat binary exposure cost

Take n=2, put T at all four square vertices, and add identical

    A_r=g+r(T-g),  a=r^d V,  0<r<=1,

at p=(-1,1) and p'=(1,-1). The base hull is exactly the triangle

    z_1<=1, z_2<=1, z_1+z_2>=0.

Its integer points are exactly the four square vertices and p,p'.
The two additions are exposed, so their actual fibers are A_r.
The core fibers remain T because every generator lies in T.
This is an actual full-dimensional convex source, including the
integer filling required by convexity. In particular the two
opposite additions are not forbidden by compatibility.

At the nonanchor core q=(0,0) the EXACT depth is

    A_mu((q,g))=Gamma V+2Gamma a.                   (12)

For the lower bound, the own fiber gives Gamma V. The two actual
outside thresholds are opposite about the centroid of A_r, so
the proved paired-centroid-tail theorem gives a combined cost
at least 2Gamma a for every continuous direction and every tilt.
Vertical caps include the own T and do not lower the result:
they include at least one of the two A_r, giving V+a, and
V+a>=Gamma(V+2a) because 2Gamma<1. For the matching upper bound,
the canonical caps

    lambda_i(x)-h(z_1+z_2)>=b                       (13)

capture Gamma V from q and Gamma a from each addition. The two
adjacent core caps are supporting zero-volume caps, and the
opposite core fiber is excluded. This proves (12) with all normals
and vertical cases covered. The paired-tail dependency is
candidate 732b11a769399016, Section 1.

The exposure costs at q are chi_q=a and Omega_{q,i}=a for EVERY i.
Indeed eta.p and eta.p' are opposites, while (6) would require
both to be at least rh>0 to exclude both A_r. The dual witness is
mu_p=mu_p'=1, gamma=0. Either individual fiber can be excluded by
a feasible unequal choice of eta_1,eta_2. Thus (12) is strictly
below Gamma V+chi_q when d>=2.

More explicitly, any canonical cap at (q,g) that excludes the
other core fibers and makes each addition either wholly full or
zero must pay at least a. The lambda_i range on A_r is
[b-rb,b+rh]. Opposite offsets cannot make both caps zero; a
sufficiently unequal tilt makes one wholly full and the other
zero, so this minimum is exactly a. In contrast (13) pays proper
fractions Gamma and Gamma, with total 2Gamma a<a. Taking a=tV
makes the discrepancy an exact FIRST-ORDER gap, not a remainder.

This example also has a precise global scope. If a<=rho_d V,
its true maximum is Gamma V+a, attained precisely at
((0,1),g) and ((1,0),g). Each is the anchor of one addition, so
(2) proves its lower bound. The functions

    delta_01=z_1+1-z_2,  delta_10=1-z_1+z_2

are -1 on their owned addition and positive on every other base
except their own anchor. Tilts 2 give mass Gamma V+a at that
anchor and a strict smaller cap at every noncentroid there.
At q, the d+1 caps (13) cover its whole fiber with budgets
Gamma V+2Gamma a<Gamma V+a. At (1,1), delta=2-z_1-z_2 isolates
the own canonical caps of mass Gamma V. The two outside bases
are exposed and have vertical isolating caps of mass a.
These are a finite original-cap upper cover and complete the
global and uniqueness-set claims. In particular this is not an
OC counterexample or a claim that the nonanchor candidate wins.

The new obstruction is precise: even for actual compatible small
additions, the first-order optimum can occur on an exposure-LP
boundary where multiple small traces remain proper. Base signs
and weighted binary exclusion costs alone discard that information.

## 6. Exact verification scope

../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_multiple_shell_anchor_credit_and_exposure_lp.py uses the
Python standard library and rational polygon clipping. It verifies
17496 actual six-base cap inequalities, 96 exact two-variable LP
tests, 4200 aggregate-anchor cap inequalities, and 20856 explicit
base-exposure inequalities. It also checks the finite matching
upper covers and the exact partial-versus-binary trace gap.
The all-direction and all-dimension conclusions follow from the
proofs above and the cited paired-tail theorem, not from the finite
normal screen.
